intent: Make shell coverage measure the tests instead of the instrument: correct kcov's denominator (continuation lines of multi-line quoted arguments are not statements) and replace its unreliable numerator with a PS4 xtrace, so libs stop being capped at numbers no test can move.
scope: meta/scripts/shell_coverage_jail.sh - runs two passes and reconciles their failures
meta/scripts/lib/shell_coverage_case_runner.sh - per-pass case execution; BASH_ENV trace delivery
meta/scripts/shell_coverage_report.py - union arithmetic and source resolution
docs/kcov-under-report.md - records the fix and the three root causes
Non-goal: wiring the gate into pre-commit/pre-push/CI (waits for the allowlist to reach zero)
Non-goal: excluding `done < <(...)` from the denominator (fail-open direction; needs per-line justification)
changes: Two passes over the same cases in two fresh namespaces: kcov's ptrace and bash's xtrace are mutually exclusive, measured A/B -- under SHELLOPTS=xtrace every kcov hit collapses from 1 to 0. Pass one supplies the instrumentable line set, pass two the executed set.

Coverage = (PS4-traced lines UNION kcov hits) INTERSECT (kcov line set MINUS continuation lines). The trace deliberately does not supply the denominator: it can only report lines that ran, so trace-as-denominator would make every subject 100% and gate on nothing.

Trace delivered via a BASH_ENV file that assigns PS4 and runs `set -x` inside each shell. Required because bash under `unshare --map-root-user` runs privileged and DISCARDS an inherited PS4 (falling back to the default '+ ', losing the file:line prefix entirely), and because `set -x` does not propagate to child processes while SHELLOPTS is readonly inside bash.
Continuation lines detected by tracking single/double quote state across the source, honouring backslash escapes in double quotes only and treating an unquoted # as end-of-line.
Source path resolved from the trace's ${BASH_SOURCE} or a unique repo search, because kcov records only a bare basename; an ambiguous basename yields no exclusion rather than a wrong guess.
The trace pass failing more cases than the kcov pass is a hard error: a partially-traced case under-reports and looks exactly like the defect being fixed.
Traced lines absent from kcov's line set are counted and reported rather than silently dropped -- a non-zero count is a third defect the design cannot correct for.

verification.evidence: dot_resolver_install.sh: 39/39 lines = 100.00%, exit 0. Acceptance baseline unchanged by the instrument change.

rpi_nc_ca.sh: 73/73 lines = 100.00%, exit 0 -- was 72/73 = 98.63%. Line 141 was lost to cross-process contagion from test_dwm_config.sh; the trace pass has no kcov in it to contaminate. This is the discriminating check that the numerator fix landed.

35/73 = 47.95% -> 65/66 = 98.48%. Denominator lost exactly the 7 continuation lines 64-66 and 98-101; numerator rose from 35 to 65. Remaining uncovered line 39 is a `done < <(...)`, left in the denominator deliberately.
10/88 = 11.36% -> 85/88 = 96.59%. The lib was never test-limited; its 29 assertions already passed.

verification.command: python3 -m coverage run --branch --source=meta/scripts -m pytest (the two new test modules); coverage report -m
verification.evidence: meta/scripts/lib/shell_coverage_lines.py 53 stmts 38 branches 100%; meta/scripts/shell_coverage_report.py 61 stmts 28 branches 100%.

verification.command: pre-commit run --files (the seven touched code files)
verification.evidence: All hooks pass. Three real lint findings were fixed at source, not suppressed: EXE001 (shebang without exec bit), PLR2004 (magic argv index named _ARGV_WITH_TRACE), E501 (long test signatures wrapped).

risks: Every measurement now runs the suite twice, so an --all sweep takes roughly double the wall time. That is why the gate belongs in CI rather than a commit hook.
xtrace is slower than an untraced run, so a case near its --timeout under kcov can exceed it under trace. This fails loudly via the pass-failure reconciliation rather than silently under-reporting.
A subject that runs `set +x`, inspects $-, or opens fd 199 would corrupt its own trace. Neither construct exists in any current subject (grepped), and fd 199 was chosen over a low fd for this reason.

The continuation-line detector is a quote-state scanner, not a bash parser. Over-detection would inflate coverage; it was validated against dwm_config.sh, where it flags exactly the 7 known lines and nothing else.
rollback: git revert the commit; the previous instrument is self-contained in the same five files.

After rollback, re-measure dot_resolver_install.sh (expect 39/39) and rpi_nc_ca.sh (expect the old 72/73 = 98.63%) to confirm the old behaviour is back, and restore the allowlist entries for any lib cleared on the strength of the new numbers.
